THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.133/2010 dated 12.07.2013 by the Court of Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Channagiri, (SCCH-13),
seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case are that, on 03.01.2010 at about 1.30 p.m., when the appellant/claimant-Sri.Santhosh Naik and one Shashikumar were proceeding on the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA.27/E-4654 from Kadarnahalli to Thyavanagi and when they reached near Arehalli Village, the Respondent No.1/driver of the tractor bearing No.KA.17/TA.8008 came in rash and negligent manner NC: 2023:KHC:25131 with high speed and dashed against the said motor cycle from back side.

As a result, both the rider and pillion rider fell down, at that time, the respondent No.4, the driver of another tractor bearing No.KA.17/T.5919 came from Channagiri side in rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed to the appellant-rider and pillion rider.
In the result, the appellant/claimant sustained injuries to his right knee, right eye, shoulder, tooth on right side, chest, back bone, right thigh, waist and other parts of the body.
Hence, he filed a claim petition against the respondents claiming compensation.

6. Heard the learned counsel appearing on both sides and perused the records.
7.

The learned counsel for the appellant/claimant while reiterating the grounds urged in the memorandum of appeal, contended that, considering NC: 2023:KHC:25131 the nature of injuries suffered by the appellant/claimant, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under various heads is on the lower side and sought for enhancement of the same.
8. Learned counsel for the Respondent Nos. 3 & 6/Insurance Company sought to justify the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.
9. The quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'Injuries, pain and suffering' at Rs.1,00,000/- is found to be proper and justified and hence, the same is kept intact.

10. From the evidence of the Doctor, it is proved that the claimant had suffered the following disabilities:-
i) Patient walks with limb and with a support of walking stick and knee brace NC:
2023:KHC:25131 ii) Healed surgical scars are present on the Knee, lateral aspect of lower thigh iii) Gross wasting of right thigh muscles iv) Flexon deformity of right knee by 150.

v) Tenderness around knee, lower third thigh vi) Anterior-Posterior and Medio Lateral instability of the knee vii) Muscle power of thigh muscles grade 3/5 viii) Operative scar over right clavicular ix) Wasting of muscles around shoulder x) Restriction of Range of Movements of shoulder xi) Decreased muscle power around shoulder about Radiologically:

sentences.text: The Doctor deposed that the claimant has suffered 79% of permanent physical disability in respect of right limb and 18% in respect of right upper limb.
The Medical Board has assessed the permanent physical disability to the tune of 60% and the Tribunal has taken the disability at 30%.
The claimant is an agriculturist and milk vendor by profession.

Exs.P16 to P18 prove that the claimant was supplying milk to the Milk Producers Co- operative Society, which shows that the claimant was supplying the milk to the society approximately 240 liters per month.

Therefore,
certainly the type of grievous injuries including fractural injuries would affect the earning capacity of the claimant substantially.
Considering the evidence of the Doctor, as discussed above, the claimant had suffered 79% of permanent physical disability to right lower limb and 18% to the right upper limb.

Therefore,
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:25131 half of the body is severely affected.
The aspect of physical disability and the functional disability are different.
In this regard, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Rajkumar Vs. Ajaykumar and Another [2011) 1 SCC 343], has laid down the principle of law regarding how to assess the functional disability.

sentences.text: The Doctor can only say physical disability as to whether it is permanent or partial disability.
But, the Court has to assess the functional disability based on the profession/avocation, age, income of any claimant and also the nature and gravity of injuries suffered by him/her.

Therefore, it is just and proper to take the functional disability at 60%
which would affect his earning capacity.
12. Further the Tribunal has taken the income of the claimant at Rs.4,000/- per month as Notional Income.
The Notional Income has to be taken in the absence of proof of income and avocation.
The claimant has produced Exs.P16 to P18, which are the Cards issued by the Milk Producers Co-operative Society, which prove that - 11 - Sri Santosh Naik vs Sri B Nagaraj on 19 July, 2023

It is a common experience that the milk is not only supplied to the society, but also sold in the open market and delivered to public to their houses.
Apart from that, the claimant is claiming that he is an agriculturist and he was looking after the agricultural lands standing in the name of his father.
Therefore considering all these facts and circumstances, it is just and proper to consider the income of the claimant at Rs.6,500/- per month.
13. From the above discussion, it is clear that, the claimant had suffered physical disability considerably, which would affect the future prospects of his life.

Therefore, as per the Division Bench decision of this court in MFA Nos. 103807/2016 c/w. MFA 103835/2016 [New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Abdul and others] rendered on 27.05.2022, certain income has to be added considering the age of the claimant, by following the principles laid-down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:25131 reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

sentences.text: The claimant was aged about 19 years.

Therefore, 40% of the income of the claimant is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life,
which works out to Rs.2,600/-.
Then the monthly income of the claimant would work-out to Rs.6500+Rs.2600=Rs.9100/-.
The multiplier applicable is '18'.
Therefore, the loss of future income due to disability suffered by the claimant including loss of future prospects, is hereby re-
assessed and quantified at Rs.11,79,360/- (Rs.8900x12x18x60/100).
14. The Tribunal has awarded a meager compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head of Loss of Amenities.

Considering the nature and gravity of injuries sustained by the claimant and the disability suffered by him, as discussed above, the appellant/claimant has lost happiness and suffered discomfort to certain extent at the young age of 19 years, which cannot be quantified by way of money.

Therefore, the compensation of Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head of Loss of - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:25131 Amenities is on lower side and hence the same is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
15.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.70,000/- jointly towards medical expenses,
hospitalization charges and incidental charges viz., the Food and Nourishment, attendant charges,
conveyance etc. including physiotherapy, which is on lower side.
The claimant has produced the bills pertaining the medicines and hospitalization charges for a sum of Rs.70,000/-.

The claimant was admitted in the hospital as inpatient for a period of 60 days and he has spent considerable amount towards incidental charges like conveyance, food and nourishment, physiotherapy etc. and also spent considerable amount for follow-up treatment including physiotherapy.
Therefore, it is just and appropriate to award an additional amount of Rs.70,000/- under the head of Incidental Expenses.
As such, the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,40,000/- under the head of Medical expenses and incidental expenses.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the claimant had undergone a surgery for knee injury suffered by him in the accident in question after discharge from the hospital and for that he spent a sum of Rs.1,50,000/-.
But, no evidence is produced to substantiate the said contention.

However, it is noticed that, in list of injuries and disabilities list extracted above, there is a mention about the certain injuries suffered by the claimant to his right leg knee and also about the scar of stitches on right knee.
Therefore it is evident that the claimant has undergone some surgery to his right knee.

Therefore, though there is no material with regard to the claimant undergoing knee surgery after some time, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the claimant, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.50,000/-
towards additional future Medical Expenses.

17. Considering the nature of injuries and disabilities suffered by the claimant, it can be assessed that, he might not have attended his regular work for a period of six months and as such, he suffered economical - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:25131 loss to some extent.

Therefore, he is entitled for a sum of Rs.39,000/-
(Rs.6500x6) under the head of 'Loss of Income during laid-up period'.
18. Further, it is to be noted here that the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.9,400/- towards simple injuries.
Since this is already included in the compensation awarded towards injuries, pain and sufferings the same does not survive for consideration and hence, the same is set aside.
19. Learned counsel for the Respondents No.3 & 6/Insurance company submitted that the interest may be waived off for the delayed period of 82 days in filing the appeal.

20. In the above facts and circumstances, the appellant/claimant is entitled to the revised compensation as under:-
